result.title: Preface
result.summary: The document outlines the contents of INREV’s Due Diligence Questionnaire (DDQ) for Non-Listed Real Estate Investment Vehicles, covering a Vehicle Fact Sheet, Investment Manager Statement, preliminary and advanced reviews of strategy, assets, terms, processes, staff, fees, investors, platform and track record, and supplementary operational topics including reporting, risk, security, continuity, regulation, governance and ESG. Introduced in 2007 and updated through 2018, the DDQ standardises investor access to vehicle, manager and operational information. Its three phases support initial shortlisting, selection for operational due diligence, and completion of operational review, with sensitive information shared later. Data-room materials should be provided or attached if no room exists, and relevant extra documents may be referenced. It also accommodates joint ventures, separate accounts and club deals, but does not replace meetings or other detailed due diligence. Answers should be clear, precise and cross-referenced, using INREV definitions. Related questionnaires cover fund-of-funds, multi-manager and debt vehicles. Use the questionnaire complete and unamended; INREV disclaims responsibility for its completion or corrections.

result.title: Disclaimer
result.summary:
Disclaimer
This questionnaire contains a disclaimer because the document will amount to a promotion. Therefore, the completed questionnaire can only be sent to restricted categories of investors. Each investment manager will need to ensure that the questionnaire contains the appropriate disclaimer.
It is recommended that the investment manager reprints the disclaimer contained in their PPM, if applicable, and upon which they have obtained relevant legal advice.
INREV is not in a position to give legal advice in relation to appropriate disclaimers. However, INREV’s view is that responses to the Due Diligence Questionnaire for Non-Listed Real Estate Investment Vehicles have the same status as the PPM.
Due Diligence Questionnaire for Non-Listed Real Estate Investment Vehicles
4

result.title: Vehicle Fact Sheet
result.summary: A vehicle fact sheet for a due diligence questionnaire on non-listed real estate investment vehicles, covering general vehicle and manager details; structure, domicile, style, legal form, closing and termination dates; target returns, strategy, size, leverage, regions, sectors and benchmark; reporting currency, NAV, GAV, accounting standard, INREV compliance and investor type; and investor numbers, minimum investment and manager co-investment. Notes define vehicle types (fund, separate account, club deal, joint venture or other), structures (open- or closed-end), styles (core, core plus, value add, opportunistic or other), and request brief details of strategic themes or subsectors.

result.title: Investment Manager Statement
result.summary:
Investment Manager Statement
This statement should be short, no more than one page, and outline what distinguishes the investment manager and vehicle from competitors and competing offerings. The statement should not be a direct copy of information contained in the vehicle marketing documents or the PPM but should be a short, unique summary of factual information that can be substantiated within the DDQ or other supporting documents. For further guidance on content, please see Appendix I.
Due Diligence Questionnaire for Non-Listed Real Estate Investment Vehicles

result.title: 1 Preliminary Stage
result.summary: The preliminary stage examines the vehicle’s investment strategy, objectives, themes, rationale, legal/PPM restrictions and guidelines, leverage and debt-management policies, controls, and debt facilities. It requests portfolio composition or seed-asset details and any realised returns. Principal terms cover investor approval rights and thresholds, governing-document references, side-letter provisions and disclosure practices, and ESG, ethics, and conflicts policies. Investment and asset-management questions address portfolio construction, approvals, advisory committees, risk integration, sourcing, deal screening and allocation, investment-period extensions, exits, liquidity, redemptions, and currency hedging. Staffing requests include organisation charts, senior personnel biographies and responsibilities, fee and expense details, TER calculations, formation costs, and the five largest investors. The manager platform section covers organisational structure, group offices and staffing, real-estate personnel by office, three-year AUM by vehicle type, and active or fundraising vehicles. Track-record information is requested for comparable vehicles or mandates, including whether performance was audited.

nodes.summary: The preliminary-stage questionnaire requests a brief account of the vehicle’s investment strategy, objectives, key themes, and rationale. It asks for legal-documentation or PPM limits, with relevant sections cited and each identified as a restriction or guideline, covering investment style, geography, sectors, tenant covenant, development, investment size, use of real estate funds/equities/debt/derivatives, liquidity, in-house vehicles, lender exposure, and any other limits. A copy of the PPM should be placed in the Data Room. The questionnaire also requests the vehicle’s leverage and debt-management strategy, including vehicle- and asset-level short- and long-term debt, targets, restrictions, controls such as LTV, interest-coverage and debt-service-coverage ratios, collateralised debt, and the number of debt facilities.

nodes.summary: A due diligence questionnaire on principal terms for non-listed real estate investment vehicles. It asks whether investor approval is required for changes to investment strategy, vehicle term, investment period, leverage limits, manager replacement, or investment-manager change of control; the approval threshold; legal-document/PPM references; and relevant provision extracts or comments. It also covers side-letter provisions on vehicle timing or termination, acquisitions/disposals outside strategy, manager remuneration, waterfall, no-fault divorce, for-cause removal, and other matters. Additional policies include ESG, code of ethics, and conflicts of interest. Respondents indicate whether side letters are disclosed to all investors or only investors above a commitment threshold, identify any other disclosure arrangements, state whether historic side letters are included, and provide comments.

Exit questions distinguish open-ended vehicles (subscription/redemption pricing and discretion to vary it) from closed-ended vehicles (extension approvals and exit strategy, including full liquidation). It asks for fund management fee timing, services, calculation basis and level; details of all other fees and their effect on gross-to-net returns; INREV TER estimates or actual figures based on NAV and GAV, with and without performance fees, and calculation methodology; and vehicle formation costs and whether they are written off or capitalised and amortised. result.title: 2 Advanced Stage
result.summary: The section assesses the vehicle’s investment strategy, allocation and return targets, research, financing, leverage, covenant governance, guarantees, credit facilities and hedging. It requests existing-vehicle reports and loss/write-down remediation and recovery estimates, or seed-asset information. Principal terms include ethics, manager removal, indemnification, key-person events, conflicts, exclusivity and reinvestment. It covers investment sourcing, underwriting, due diligence, committees, co-investments, asset monitoring, wind-up, cash controls, capital calls and distributions. Staff topics include departures, team tenure, succession, compensation, outside interests, conflicts and dedicated specialist resources. Fees, expenses, waterfall and carry mechanics, oversight, leakage scenarios and performance calculations are examined. Investor arrangements include share classes, side letters, liability, meetings, defaults, confidentiality, pricing, equalisation and KYC/AML. The manager’s ownership, recruitment, staff development, financial reporting and business strategy are reviewed, along with explanations of worst-performing vehicles and the continued involvement of responsible individuals.

nodes.summary: Requests the vehicle and manager’s Code of Ethics; details of no-fault and for-cause manager removal, including triggers, voting thresholds and rights, restrictions, cause determination, effects on co-investment, and any compensation (base or performance fees). It also covers indemnification and exculpation, exceptions for negligence, fraud, wilful misconduct, criminal acts, material conduct breaches or other matters, with comments and legal-document references. The questionnaire asks whether key-man provisions apply during the investment period, replacement period, or at all times, and the consequences of a key-person event, including suspension or investor approval of a replacement. It asks about conflicts-of-interest provisions, comments, and who receives disclosures. Finally, it addresses deal-flow exclusivity and competing vehicles during the investment period, and reinvestment of principal, profits, or income and the applicable period.

nodes.summary: The questionnaire requests information on the investment and asset-management process: how new markets and sectors are assessed, process changes over three years, input from internal teams, investment committee membership and terms, and sample asset or transaction documents. It covers deal-flow databases and update frequency; underwriting models, assumptions and metrics for asset returns, leasing, costs, financing and refinancing; and due-diligence team roles and outsourcing. It asks about co-investment policies, approvals, joint-venture structures, partner compensation and oversight. Asset monitoring questions cover buy/hold/sell criteria, forecasting models and updates, property visits, and monitoring beyond the vehicle’s planned life. It also addresses vehicle wind-up and ongoing liabilities, prior secondary trading, cash and securities movement controls and authorizations, responsible staff and experience, expense buffers, and the frequency and notice periods for capital calls and distributions.

nodes.summary: Requests a summary budget of vehicle fees and costs, including estimates, maximum amounts, and expected development over the vehicle’s life. Requires details of the waterfall and carry structures: basis, hurdle, percentages, gross-to-net impact, overall or deal-by-deal basis, manager/investor split, reimbursement of investor fees and organisational expenses before promote, catch-up, performance fees, and clawback or escrow provisions, including whether fees are paid at the vehicle’s end. Asks who maintains investor waterfall models and how they are reviewed, approved, and audited. Also requires estimated fee-leakage scenarios for below-target, on-target, and above-target performance, plus worked performance-fee calculations for anticipated, under-, and over-performance.

It also asks for unit pricing at initial and subsequent closings, equalisation provisions for investors joining after launch, and responsibility for KYC and anti-money-laundering checks on subscriptions.

result.title: 3 Supplementary Stage
result.summary: The supplementary stage examines reporting, valuation policies and standards, INREV compliance, investor communications and inspection rights; risk and compliance structures, proceedings, controls, insurance and management of financial, operational and legal risks; and IT, cyber and physical security, incident response, testing, access controls, disaster recovery, business continuity and crisis preparedness. It covers regulation, AIFMD and marketing status, external audits and auditor rotation. Corporate governance topics include boards and committees, decision rights, investments and carried interest, conflicts, and selection, oversight and cybersecurity expectations for service providers. ESG coverage includes policies, oversight, reporting, standards, indicators and initiatives. A Data Room checklist identifies preliminary, advanced and supplementary materials to provide or reference. The appendix guides an investment-manager statement covering history, ownership, strategy, track record, operations, governance, ESG, valuation, credentials and other information, and provides a vehicle portfolio schedule for assets, financing, covenants and performance, with definitions of key metrics.

nodes.summary: This section asks about material disputes concerning the vehicle’s documentation or operations and any qualifications to its annual accounts. It covers the valuation policy and frequency for real estate and secured loans; whether valuations are external or internal, investor rights to appoint external valuers, internal valuers’ identities and experience, events prompting valuation changes, and valuer appointment and reappointment periods. It asks which accounting and valuation standards apply; the vehicle’s module-by-module INREV Guidelines compliance percentage, explanations for departures, and whether it provides an INREV NAV. It also requests samples of investor communications and reports, reporting frequency and deadlines, whether all investors receive the same information simultaneously, whether reports can be tailored to client needs, and investors’ rights to inspect books and records or commission a third-party audit, including the relevant document clause.

nodes.summary: The section requests information on risk management and compliance processes, including team structure, reporting lines, issue escalation, and—where AIFMD applies—the risk management policy in the Data Room. It asks about past, current, or pending criminal, civil, regulatory, or similar proceedings involving the firm, affiliates, or principals. It requests an internal controls report and details of insurance coverage, including professional indemnity, with a Data Room schedule showing coverage levels, providers, adequacy, and claims. It also asks how risks and related controls are managed for JV partners, debt, credit, interest rates, currency, fraud, litigation, tax and legal matters, regulatory matters, and cash transfers, and whether the firm has a dedicated internal audit function at group or local-entity level.

nodes.summary: The questionnaire assesses IT, cyber and physical security practices for non-listed real estate investment vehicles, including security certifications, board oversight, documented cyber incident response plans and material incidents in the past three years. It asks about antivirus requirements for devices, staff security training and phishing tests, the frequency of vulnerability assessments and penetration tests, and any critical or high-risk findings unresolved for over six months. It also covers access to an external cyber security specialist during incidents, controls on server and communications room access, and whether permanent staff are on site while cleaners are working.

nodes.title: 3.7 Corporate Governance
nodes.summary: The section covers completion of the INREV corporate governance self-assessment and governance of boards and committees, including selection, composition, terms, investor and independent representation, manager roles, reserved decisions, voting, investment committee responsibilities, and protections for non-executive officers. It requests details of manager, personnel and committee members’ investments and carried-interest arrangements, investment retention and transfer restrictions, and treatment of departing team members. It addresses conflict-prevention protocols, recusals, approval processes, and potential conflicts involving allocations, successor vehicles, affiliates, mandates, transactions, loans and refinancing. It also examines third-party service providers’ roles, contacts, duties, independence, selection and due diligence, investor approval of replacements, monitoring, accountability, provider changes, reasons for non-use, cybersecurity requirements, and credit-product ratings and documentation.

nodes.title: 3.7.2 Boards and Committees
key_items: 3.7.2.3 What decisions/approvals are reserved for the boards/committees? Describe the processes and procedures in place.
3.7.2.6 Describe in which aspects of the vehicle’s investment (overall strategy, acquisitions and disposals) as well as operational activities the Investment Committee play an active role.
3.7.2.7 Is officers’ liability insurance provided to participants in any advisory committee or board of the vehicle?
3.7.2.8 Can any non-executive officer retain an external legal counsel at the expense of the vehicle?
nodes.summary: Covers the governance of boards and committees: investor selection, membership limits and terms, composition, manager participation, and whether investors can change their constitution; independent representation, non-executive appointments, and investor representation; reserved decisions and approval procedures; voting arrangements and the manager’s role in recommendations or consultation; whether the investment committee is vehicle-specific and how its membership changes; its involvement in investment strategy, acquisitions, disposals, and operations; and the availability of officers’ liability insurance and vehicle-funded external legal counsel for non-executive officers.

nodes.title: 3.7.3 Alignment of Interest
key_items: 3.7.3.4 What happens with carried interest if people leave?
nodes.summary: The section requests details of commitments to the investment vehicle by the fund manager, key personnel, investment committee members, and employees, including each person’s name, funding source, amount, commitment as a percentage of net worth, proposed share of carried interest, role, key-person status, transferability, and comments. It asks whether the manager will retain its investment throughout the vehicle’s life and, if not, what restrictions apply to syndicating, selling, encumbering, or transferring investments, including the basis and whether terms match those for other investors. It also asks how carried interest is distributed among team members and, where relevant, the parent company or other entities, and what happens to carried interest when team members leave.

nodes.title: 3.7.4 Potential Conflicts of Interest
key_items: 3.7.4.2 Do matters involving conflicts of interest require approval by: a Investors;
nodes.summary: Requests the conflicts-of-interest protocol, if available in the Data Room; measures to prevent conflicts; and whether conflicted parties are excluded from board or investment committee discussions. Asks which parties must approve conflicts: investors, advisory board, non-executive board, fund manager/GP, or others. Seeks the approach to conflicts involving allocation among vehicles or mandates with overlapping strategies, timing of successor vehicles, commitments to or dealings with affiliates, separate-account mandates, sales or purchases between vehicles/accounts managed by the fund manager, loans and refinancing of assets managed by the same manager, and any other issues.

nodes.title: 3.7.5 Third-Party Service Providers
key_items: 3.7.5.2 Describe your approval/due diligence process for the selection of service providers. Does the vehicle require the prior approval of investors with any replacement of service provider?
3.7.5.3 Describe your on-going due diligence/monitoring procedures for all service providers. Who is responsible for this function?
3.7.5.4 What reasons have you found to prevent you working with service providers in the past?
3.7.5.5 Discuss any changes in service providers in the last five years.
3.7.5.7 Are any of your credit products rated by rating agencies? Are the duties involved defined in the real estate debt vehicle documentation?
nodes.summary: The questionnaire asks whether the real estate vehicle uses third-party providers (such as custodians, paying or administration agents, and transfer agents) and, for each, requests its role and contact details, duties, start date, firm affiliations, compliance with independent standards, and clarification of accountability (presumed to rest with the investment manager). It also asks about provider selection and due diligence, investor approval for replacements, ongoing monitoring and responsibility, reasons for declining or being unable to work with providers, provider changes over the past five years, cybersecurity contract requirements and the personnel monitoring them, and whether credit products are rated and related duties are defined in the vehicle documentation.

nodes.title: 3.8 Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Issues
key_items: 3.8.3 Who is responsible for coordinating the monitoring of ESG issues at vehicle and organisation level?
3.8.4 Describe the process and frequency used to report ESG issues into senior management and to the investors.
3.8.5 Does the vehicle have an Environmental Management System (EMS)? What aspects are covered by the EMS?
3.8.6 Is the vehicle’s ESG report(s) in line with the INREV sustainability reporting recommendations?
3.8.9 Does the scope of the policy and management system include contracted parties and suppliers?
3.8.10 Does the vehicle and organisation operate in jurisdictions that have not ratified ILO core conventions?
3.8.11 What indicators are used to measure social performances?
nodes.summary: The section asks about ESG practices at the investment vehicle and organizational levels: GRESB participation, scores and trends, or alternative ESG indicators; how environmental, social and governance policies, including ethics, inform strategic decisions; responsibility for monitoring ESG; and reporting processes and frequency for management and investors. It also covers whether an Environmental Management System exists and its scope, alignment of ESG reports with INREV recommendations, reporting standards used, standards followed for social policies, inclusion of contractors and suppliers, operations in jurisdictions that have not ratified ILO core conventions, social performance indicators, and details of three notable ESG initiatives.

nodes.title: Data Room
nodes.summary: The Data Room table asks users to mark whether requested information is included, cite the PPM, or note if the Data Room is unavailable and information is supplied separately. Preliminary-phase items include the PPM, deal allocation policy, vehicle personnel and senior-staff biographies, organisational and real-estate structure charts, and a chart showing senior staff’s place in the wider group. Advanced-phase materials include gross-to-net returns, strategy research, an electronic financial model, applicable annual/interim reports, code of ethics, investment committee members and biographies, sample underlying-asset documents, a deal-flow database screenshot, and the manager’s two years of consolidated financial statements and annual reports, plus broker reports if applicable. Supplementary items include communications and reports, applicable AIFMD/CSSF risk policy, internal-controls report, insurance schedule, INREV governance self-assessment, conflicts protocol, and third-party service-provider list. The table associates these items with questionnaire references numbered 1.1.1.3 through 3.7.5.1.

nodes.title: Appendix
key_items: I. Investment Manager Statement Guidance
II. Composition of the portfolio for the subject vehicle (related to Question 1.2.1)
nodes.summary: The appendix provides guidance for an investment manager statement, noting its themes are non-exhaustive. It covers the manager’s inception and history, ownership, offices and local presence, AUM and currency/date, scope, investment beliefs, track record and relevant funds; and its products and services, operations and outsourcing, research, investment process, risk management, governance, ESG, valuation, property management, licenses, standards, certifications and memberships (including INREV, GRESB, PRI and RICS). It also requests a website link and additional information. A portfolio schedule for the subject vehicle lists assets/SPVs, location, sector, owner-occupancy, acquisition/exit dates, price, equity invested and totals, defining FMV and NOI. Financing fields include lenders, loan amounts/currency, maturity, margins, amortization and all-in interest. Covenant and performance fields include LTV, current and covenant ratios, FMV, projected gross/net IRR and multiples, and ICR/DSCR; abbreviations are defined.
